title: How the holiday 2022 winter storm confounded grid operators' forecast models
why: A December 2022 winter storm pushed US grid demand past what forecasts predicted, with error rates of up to 9% against the usual target of 3%. In Texas the next-day peak forecast was 67,775 MW and demand came in 8% higher, at 73,658 MW.
credit: Image: 101cats via Getty Images, via S&P Global

title: Heat and power: Impacts of the 2025 heatwave in Europe
why: In the 2025 European heatwave, daily power demand rose by up to 14% in Spain, and average daily prices rose by 106% to 175% in Poland, France and Germany. Demand moves like this are what a day-ahead forecast has to anticipate.
credit: Image: Martin Bond, Alamy, via Ember

title: Electricity load forecasting under extreme heat and cold waves
why: The authors report that load forecasting models trained mostly on ordinary weather often fail in heat and cold waves. Their analysis puts the extra cost of each megawatt-hour under-forecast a day ahead, in one extreme-weather period, at about 449 USD.
credit: Fig. 1, Lu et al., Nature Communications (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
